title: Amplitude-qualified heart-rate reversals fail a primary heart-failure transfer test and are sensitive to timestamp resolution
abstract: A frozen logistic model trained on 33 chfdb/nsrdb recordings was tested on 83 chf2db/nsr2db recordings. Adding amplitude-qualified NN reversals to mean NN, SDNN, RMSSD and pNN50 changed external AUC from 0.7931 to 0.7567 (paired bootstrap delta -0.0364, 95% interval -0.0862 to 0.0070) and increased log loss by 0.0217. Harmonizing timestamps to 128 Hz reversed the discovery association and reduced incremental differences to near zero. No robust incremental biomarker advantage was established. Separate source cohorts provide external-dataset validation, but enrollment overlap cannot be definitively excluded. Author self-checks and a byte-identical clean numerical rerun are supplied.
